items.title: 2.2.3 Intersection of a Linear Function and a Quadratic Function (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Ab tak humne seedhi lines ka milna dekha. Is sabaq mein ek seedhi line aur ek parabola (quadratic function ka U jaisa graph) ka milna dekhenge. Yahan ek nayi baat hai: milne ke points do bhi ho sakte hain, ek bhi, aur bilkul nahin bhi.

Kitab kehti hai: ek line aur ek parabola ya to do points par milte hain, ya ek point par, ya bilkul nahin milte. Agar do solutions hon to system ke do points of intersection hain. Ek solution ka matlab hai sirf ek milne ka point; is surat mein line parabola ki tangent (sirf chhoo kar guzarne wali line) ho sakti hai. Aur agar koi solution na ho to line aur parabola aapas mein milte hi nahin.

blocks.alt: Three panels, each with x and y axes and an upward parabola. Two Solutions: a line cuts the parabola at two dots. One Solution: a line touches the parabola at one dot. No Solutions: a line passes the parabola without meeting it.
blocks.caption: Figure: a line and a parabola with two, one or no points of intersection (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne figure ke darmiyani hisse par "One Solutions" likha hai. Ek hi solution ho to sahi lafz "One Solution" (singular) hai; humari figure mein yahi likha hai. Baaqi do labels "Two Solutions" aur "No Solutions" theek hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Quadratic function \(y = ax^{2} + bx + c\) (jahan \(a \ne 0\)) ka graph U jaisa curve hota hai jise parabola kehte hain. \(a > 0\) ho to yeh upar ki taraf khulta hai (pyaale ki tarah), aur \(a < 0\) ho to neeche ki taraf (ulte pyaale ki tarah). Is ka mor wala point vertex kehlata hai, jo \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\) par hota hai.
Tangent woh line hai jo curve ko ek point par sirf chhoo kar guzar jaye, kaate nahin.
Sirf 0, 1 ya 2 points hi kyun? Kyun ke jab hum line ka \(y\) parabola ki equation mein rakhte hain to \(x\) ki ek quadratic equation banti hai. Aur quadratic equation ke ya to do real roots hote hain, ya ek (dohraya hua), ya koi real root nahin; yeh discriminant \(b^{2} - 4ac\) ke positive, zero ya negative hone par munhasir hai. Har real root ek milne ka point deta hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Upar wali figure ke teesre hisse mein line parabola ke neeche se guzar rahi hai. Agar is line ko thora thora upar sarkaate jaayein to kya hoga? (Jawab: pehle woh parabola ko ek point par chhooyegi, yani tangent banegi, aur phir aur upar jaane par do points par kaatne lagegi. Yani teeno cases ek hi line ke alag alag maqam hain.)

blocks.title: Example 9
blocks.problem: Solve the linear function \(y = -x + 3\) and quadratic function \(y = x^{2} - 6x + 3\) graphically.
steps:
Given: linear function \(y = -x + 3\) aur quadratic function \(y = x^{2} - 6x + 3\).
To find: woh points jahan dono graphs milte hain (yani system ke solutions).
Method: sab se pehle hum dekhte hain ke humein do graphs banane hain: ek seedhi line aur ek parabola. Line ke liye do intercepts kaafi hain. Parabola ke liye teen cheezein chahiye: \(y\)-intercept, \(x\)-intercepts aur vertex (mor wala point). Phir dono ko ek hi axes par bana kar milne ke points parhenge, aur aakhir mein algebra se tasdeeq.

Step 1: Line \(y = -x + 3\) ke intercepts
\[x = 0:\ y = 3\]
\[y = 0:\ 0 = -x + 3 \Rightarrow x = 3\]
Yani line \((3, 0)\) aur \((0, 3)\) se guzarti hai.
Kyun: seedhi line ke liye do points kaafi hain, aur intercepts sab se aasan do points hain kyun ke un mein ek coordinate zero hota hai.

Step 2: Parabola ka \(y\)-intercept
\[y = x^{2} - 6x + 3 \quad \text{...(i)}\]
(i) mein \(x = 0\) rakhein: \(y = 3\), is liye \((0, 3)\) \(y\)-intercept hai.
Kyun: \(y\)-axis par \(x = 0\) hota hai. Ghor karein: line ka \(y\)-intercept bhi \((0, 3)\) tha! Yani yeh point dono graphs par hai; humein ek milne wala point yahin mil gaya.

Step 3: Parabola ke \(x\)-intercepts
(i) mein \(y = 0\) rakhein:
\[0 = x^{2} - 6x + 3\]
Quadratic formula, \(a = 1, b = -6, c = 3\) ke saath:
\[x = \dfrac{-(-6) \pm \sqrt{(-6)^{2} - 4(1)(3)}}{2(1)}\]
\[x = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 12}}{2}\]
\[x = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{24}}{2}\]
Kyun: \(x^{2} - 6x + 3\) poore numbers mein factorize nahin hota (aise do numbers nahin jin ka product 3 aur sum \(-6\) ho). Is liye quadratic formula \(x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^{2} - 4ac}}{2a}\) lagaya, jo har quadratic equation par chalta hai.
Dhyan dein: \(-b = -(-6) = +6\), aur \((-6)^{2} = +36\). Square hamesha positive hota hai.

Step 4: Roots ko simplify karein
\[\sqrt{24} = \sqrt{4 \times 6} = 2\sqrt{6}\]
\[x = \dfrac{6 \pm 2\sqrt{6}}{2} = 3 \pm \sqrt{6}\]
\[x = 3 - \sqrt{6},\ 3 + \sqrt{6}\]
\[x \approx 0.6,\ 5.4\]
Is liye \((0.6, 0)\) aur \((5.4, 0)\) parabola ke \(x\)-intercepts hain.
Kyun: \(24 = 4 \times 6\) aur \(\sqrt{4} = 2\), is liye \(\sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6}\). Phir numerator ke dono terms ko 2 se divide kiya. Graph par lagane ke liye decimal chahiye: \(\sqrt{6} \approx 2.449\), to \(3 - 2.449 \approx 0.55 \approx 0.6\) aur \(3 + 2.449 \approx 5.45 \approx 5.4\) (ek decimal tak, jaise kitab ne diya).

Step 5: Parabola ka vertex \((h, k)\)
\[h = -\dfrac{b}{2a} = -\dfrac{-6}{2(1)} = 3\]
\[k = (3)^{2} - 6(3) + 3\]
\[k = 9 - 18 + 3 = -6\]
Yani vertex \((3, -6)\) hai.
Kyun: vertex parabola ka mor (turning point) hai. Yahan \(a = 1\) positive hai, is liye parabola upar ki taraf khulta hai (U ki shakal) aur vertex us ka sab se neeche wala point hai. Vertex ka \(x\) formula \(-\frac{b}{2a}\) se aata hai, aur \(k\) us \(x\) par function ki value hai. Is ke baghair parabola ki gehrai ka andaza nahin hota.

Step 6: Dono graphs bana kar milne ke points parhein
Line ko \((0, 3)\) aur \((3, 0)\) se kheenchein; parabola ko \((0, 3)\), \((0.6, 0)\), \((3, -6)\) aur \((5.4, 0)\) se guzarta hua hamwaar (smooth) curve banayein (neeche graph dekhiye). Dono \((0, 3)\) aur \((5, -2)\) par milte hain.
Kyun: jo point dono graphs par ho, woh dono equations ko satisfy karta hai; wohi solution hai.

Tasdeeq:
Ab algebra se check karte hain. Milne ke points par dono \(y\) barabar hain:
\[x^{2} - 6x + 3 = -x + 3\]
\[x^{2} - 5x = 0\]
\[x(x - 5) = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0 \text{ ya } x = 5\]
\(x = 0\): \(y = 3\); \(x = 5\): \(y = -5 + 3 = -2\).
Parabola se bhi: \(5^{2} - 6(5) + 3 = 25 - 30 + 3 = -2\). Dono points pakke hain. Ghor karein ke yahan quadratic equation ke do roots aaye, isi liye milne ke do points hain.

blocks.alt: Graph of the line y = minus x + 3 and the parabola y = x squared minus 6x + 3 on a grid, x from minus 2 to 7 and y from minus 7 to 6. Dots mark (0, 3) and (5, minus 2), where they meet, the vertex (3, minus 6) and the parabola's x-intercepts near 0.6 and 5.4.
blocks.caption: Figure: y = −x + 3 and y = x² − 6x + 3 meet at (0, 3) and (5, −2) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ke graph mein \(x\)-axis par \(-2\) aur \(-1\), aur \(y\)-axis par \(-2\), minus sign ke baghair chhape hain. Yeh axes ki negative (manfi) taraf hain, is liye in ke saath minus hona chahiye. Humari figure mein sahi numbers \(-2\), \(-1\) aur \(-2\) hain.
Is tarah \((0, 3)\) aur \((5, -2)\) di gayi functions ke solutions (points of intersection) hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Parabola achha banane ka tareeqa: pehle vertex lagaiye, kyun ke wohi curve ka mor hai aur parabola us ke daayen baayen bilkul ek jaisa (symmetric) hota hai. Is misaal mein vertex \((3, -6)\) hai, is liye line \(x = 3\) parabola ka aaina (axis of symmetry) hai: \((0, 3)\) ka jora \((6, 3)\) hai, aur \((0.6, 0)\) ka jora \((5.4, 0)\). Yeh jore lagane se curve khud ba khud sahi shakal le leta hai. Aakhir mein haath halka rakh kar ek hi hamwaar line mein points ko jorein; ruler sirf seedhi line ke liye hai, parabola ke liye nahin.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai (kitab ka sawal nahin): line \(y = 2x - 1\) aur parabola \(y = x^{2}\).
Barabar rakhein: \(x^{2} = 2x - 1 \Rightarrow x^{2} - 2x + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow (x - 1)^{2} = 0\).
Sirf ek root \(x = 1\) (dohraya hua), aur \(y = 1\). Yani line parabola ko sirf \((1, 1)\) par chhooti hai: yeh tangent hai, "One Solution" wala case. Discriminant: \((-2)^{2} - 4(1)(1) = 0\).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Line aur parabola do points par, ek point par (line tangent ho) ya bilkul nahin milte.
2. Parabola banane ke liye: \(y\)-intercept (\(x = 0\)), \(x\)-intercepts (\(y = 0\), quadratic formula) aur vertex \(h = -\frac{b}{2a}\), \(k = f(h)\).
3. Graph se milne ke points parhein, phir dono equations barabar rakh kar tasdeeq karein.
4. Milne ke points ki tadaad = mili hui quadratic equation ke real roots ki tadaad.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Quadratic formula mein sign ki ghalti: \(-b = -(-6) = 6\) aur \((-6)^{2} = 36\), \(-36\) nahin.
2. \(\sqrt{24}\) ko \(2\sqrt{6}\) na banana, ya sirf ek term ko 2 se divide karna: \(\frac{6 \pm 2\sqrt{6}}{2} = 3 \pm \sqrt{6}\), dono terms divide hote hain.
3. Parabola ke \(x\)-intercepts \((0.6, 0)\), \((5.4, 0)\) ko hi jawab likh dena: jawab woh points hain jo dono graphs mein common hain, yani \((0, 3)\) aur \((5, -2)\).
4. Parabola ka neeche wala hissa nokeela (V jaisa) bana dena: vertex par bhi curve gol aur hamwaar hota hai.
